context: Known as Ayat al-Kursi ("The Throne Verse"), one of the most widely memorized verses in the Quran. It describes God's knowledge and sovereignty over all creation.
A closing verse of Surah Al-Baqarah, often cited as a reminder that no one is asked to bear more than they are able to.
From Surah Ash-Sharh. The phrase is repeated twice in the surah (verses 5 and 6), a structure often noted for its emphasis.
The second occurrence of this phrase in Surah Ash-Sharh, immediately following verse 5.
A short verse from Surah Al-Baqarah on the relationship between remembrance and gratitude.
Revealed in the context of hardship after the Battle of Uhud, addressed to a community that had suffered losses.
From Surah Ar-Ra'd, describing the effect of remembrance on the heart.
From Surah At-Talaq, part of a passage on reliance and provision.
From Surah Az-Zumar, addressed to those who fear they have gone too far in wrongdoing.
A verse in Surah Al-Baqarah, situated among verses on fasting, describing nearness in response to a question about prayer.
The beginning of Prophet Musa's prayer before addressing Pharaoh, in Surah Ta-Ha.
The prayer of Prophet Yunus (Jonah), spoken while in the belly of the whale, in Surah Al-Anbiya.
Words spoken by Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) to his sons in Surah Yusuf, after years of separation from his son.
The opening verse of Surah Ash-Sharh, a short Meccan surah addressed directly to the Prophet.
From Surah An-Nahl, on righteous action regardless of gender.
The closing verse of Surah Al-Ankabut.
From Surah Al-Baqarah, pairing patience and prayer as a means of support.
The closing verse of Surah Ali 'Imran.
A refrain repeated 31 times throughout Surah Ar-Rahman, following descriptions of different favors.
Known as Ayat an-Nur ("The Light Verse"), from Surah An-Nur, using an extended metaphor of light.
From Surah Al-Isra, on speech and conduct toward parents.
From Surah Al-Hujurat, on the diversity of peoples and tribes.
From Surah Fussilat, on responding to hostility.
From Surah Al-Baqarah, in a passage discussing obligations some found difficult.
The prayer of the young companions of the cave, in Surah Al-Kahf, as they sought refuge.
Prophet Sulaiman's (Solomon's) prayer of gratitude, in Surah An-Naml.
From Surah Ibrahim, part of a passage recounting Musa's address to his people.
From Surah Ali 'Imran, an address recognizing sovereignty over all affairs.
The closing verse of Surah Al-Hashr, listing several names traditionally understood as attributes.
The opening of Surah Al-Ikhlas, a short surah often noted for its concise structure.
The opening of Surah Al-Asr, a three-verse surah on time.
From Surah Az-Zalzalah, using the image of an atom's weight.
The opening verse of Surah Al-Qadr, referring to a specific night.
An earlier verse in Surah Al-Baqarah pairing patience and prayer.
From Surah Al-An'am, on knowledge described as unseen.
From Surah Al-A'raf, pairing fear and hope in calling upon God.
Words spoken in a cave during a journey, recounted in Surah At-Tawbah.
From Surah Al-Hijr, part of a dialogue about mercy.
From Surah Al-Furqan, describing a manner of walking and responding to others.
Part of Luqman's advice to his son, in Surah Luqman.
From Surah Al-Ahzab, a short instruction on frequent remembrance.
From Surah Saba, on spending and its return.
From Surah Ash-Shura, a short verse on gentleness.
From Surah Qaf, using the image of the jugular vein to describe nearness.
From Surah Al-Hadid, in a passage describing knowledge of creation.
From Surah Al-Insan, describing an act of giving done without expectation.
From Surah Ad-Duha, a short Meccan surah of reassurance.
The closing verse of Surah Ad-Duha, on acknowledging good received.
From Surah Al-Balad, describing struggle as part of the human condition.
A prayer recounted in Surah Ali 'Imran, asking for steadfastness after guidance.
